whyItMatters: A password reset becomes far more meaningful when the target user quickly authenticates successfully. This is one of the clearest signals that the reset was operationally used, not just configured.

threatContext.attackerBehavior: An attacker may reset a user's password and then immediately log in as that user to exercise the new access path.
threatContext.realWorldUsage: This is a classic account-takeover sequence in IAM-user environments because it ties credential manipulation directly to subsequent access.
threatContext.whyItMatters: The key split is whether this was expected self-service recovery or an external reset followed by active use.
threatContext.riskAndImpact: If missed, a reset event that initially looks routine can quickly become interactive console takeover with no timely response.

requiredLogSources: AWS CloudTrail management events for IAM
loggingRequirements: IAM reset telemetry and sign-in telemetry must both be ingested.
Sign-in events must preserve successful ConsoleLogin results.
The environment should be able to map sign-in events back to the target IAM user reliably.
limitations: Simple username extraction from sign-in events can be brittle.
Legitimate self-service resets followed by login are expected in some environments.
CloudWatch count-based approximations are not sufficient for real correlation.

enrichment.description: Determine whether the reset was self-service, delegated helpdesk, or suspicious third-party activity.
examples: workload role reset then target login
enrichment.falsePositiveReduction: Makes the correlation story much more actionable.

enrichment.description: Evaluate MFA use, first-seen source IP, geography, device fingerprint, and time-to-login.
examples: login from new country within minutes
enrichment.falsePositiveReduction: Separates routine password recovery from suspicious access activation.

enrichment.description: Classify whether the user is privileged, dormant, non-human, or otherwise unusual for console activity.
enrichment.falsePositiveReduction: Raises priority when the reset affected a user that matters more.

logicExplanation.humanReadable: This should be the high-confidence branch for password-reset abuse. The strongest implementation links UpdateLoginProfile to a successful ConsoleLogin by the same target user in a short window, then enriches the login with MFA and source context.
conditions: second eventSource equals signin.amazonaws.com and eventName equals ConsoleLogin
login user matches the target user from the reset event
logicExplanation.tuningGuidance: 1. Do not alert on either event alone. 2. Distinguish self-reset-and-login from third-party reset-and-login. 3. Escalate for no MFA, unusual source IP, and sensitive target users.
logicExplanation.whenToFire: Fire when a password reset is followed by successful console use by that same target user, especially when the reset relationship or login context is suspicious.

quality.falsePositiveRate: Low-Medium depending on self-service recovery volume and target-user context

deployment.scheduling: Best in near-real-time because the access pattern is short-window and actionable.
considerations: Use this as the high-confidence branch above baseline password resets.
